page: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is an entry-tier instance within the compute-optimized C2D family, powered by AMD EPYC 7B13 x86_64 processors. The configuration provisions 2 dedicated vCPUs backed by 1 physical core with 2 execution threads, paired with 4.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a compute-aligned 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. Cache hierarchy allocations include 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX, AES, and SHA-NI, though AVX-512 extensions are not supported. The instance features no integrated local storage and operates with zero GPU acceleration.

Benchmark measurements reflect a separation between single-thread capability and concurrent scaling. Single-core processing performs reliably, evidenced by a stress-ng single-core score of 2921.98 placing in the top 25%, alongside average single-threaded gzip compression throughput of 27.79 GB/sec. Conversely, overall throughput is bounded by the two-thread capacity. The platform yields weak to poor multi-core results, including a multi-core Geekbench score of 2013.0, a Clang compilation score of 2134.0, and lower-tier large-block memory read bandwidth of 31.59 GB/sec.

From an infrastructure efficiency standpoint, the instance delivers a low-overhead entry point for applications requiring dedicated AMD EPYC execution without paying for surplus memory capacity. The primary tradeoffs center on the small 4.0 GB memory ceiling, absence of ephemeral NVMe storage, and modest I/O bandwidth, which limits database handling to 1006.97 PassMark database operations and static web serving to 2.82 GB/sec. Appropriate workload profiles include light backend utilities, single-threaded processing queues, simple ETL scripts, and basic CI/CD jobs.
description: Google Cloud Platform c2d-highcpu-2 is a compute-optimized virtual machine equipped with 2 dedicated vCPUs operating on 1 physical AMD EPYC 7B13 core, 4.0 GB of system memory, and an x86_64 architecture. The instance provisions a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, contains no integrated GPUs, and includes no local storage. Architectural features include 32 MB of L3 cache alongside support for AES, AVX, and SHA-NI instruction sets. Synthetic testing indicates solid single-core throughput, highlighted by top-quartile stress-ng single-core scores and average single-threaded compression speeds. Conversely, overall capacity is strictly bounded by its dual-thread hardware footprint, resulting in bottom-quartile results across multi-core benchmarks, memory bandwidth tests, and database transaction workloads. The instance functions as an entry-level compute node offering low operational overhead for workloads that do not demand substantial parallel scale or memory capacity, such as lightweight backend services, single-threaded processing queues, and basic continuous integration tasks.
